title: Comparing satellite aerosol observations with ground evidence
summary: I contributed Earth-observation automation and regression analysis to a NASA DEVELOP air-quality study in Central America. Partner-supplied PM2.5 records in El Salvador enabled detailed satellite-product comparisons, while a separate CALIOP–Aqua MODIS analysis examined agreement between lidar and passive measurements of atmospheric aerosols.
role: NASA DEVELOP team researcher · Data processing and regression analysis
context: Central America · Detailed ground-station comparisons in El Salvador

image.alt: Original MODIS04 versus MODIS08 AOD and PM2.5 regression for El Salvador, 2009–2019
image.caption: Original NASA DEVELOP analysis, technical report Figure 5. El Salvador MODIS04 and MODIS08 regressions compare satellite AOD with ground-station PM2.5 over 2009–2019; reported R² values are 0.47 and 0.30 respectively.

problem: Satellite aerosol products can extend air-quality research beyond monitoring stations, but they measure atmospheric aerosols differently from ground-level particulate matter. The team needed to compare products against available station records and understand where measurements agreed, diverged or lacked coverage.
contribution: I helped develop and automate acquisition, processing and extraction of NASA Earth-observation products for ArcGIS Pro, and contributed regression analysis in R using El Salvador partner-supplied PM2.5 measurements. Across the two NASA projects, the shared processing effort handled more than 900 multidimensional files; that total is not attributed to this project alone.

approach.title: Prepare different observation products
approach.body: Automated acquisition and preprocessing of satellite and environmental files so their observations could be analyzed in ArcGIS Pro and statistical workflows. Products and measurement characteristics were specific to the air-quality study.

approach.title: Use ground observations to test associations
approach.body: Compared MODIS04, MODIS08 and VIIRS aerosol optical depth with in-situ PM2.5. El Salvador’s comparatively complete San Salvador station record supported the detailed regression comparisons.

approach.title: Keep comparison windows explicit
approach.body: Separated the 2009–2019 product regressions from the matched 47-month three-product analysis and the regional poster summaries. Different samples and temporal windows were not treated as interchangeable model scores.

approach.title: Compare independent satellite measurements
approach.body: The team paired CALIOP lidar and Aqua MODIS observations on 118 days during 2009–2019. This examined cross-sensor AOD consistency separately from the ground-station PM2.5 regressions.

outcome: The study produced original regression figures and a paired satellite time series that show both the usefulness and limits of aerosol observations for regional air-quality research. The full-period El Salvador comparisons reported R² of 0.47 for MODIS04 and 0.30 for MODIS08; these are team research results for the stated sample.
learning: The work demonstrates how data engineering and statistical comparison must be adapted to the measurement itself: a lidar profile, column aerosol estimate and ground-station concentration are related observations, but not equivalent variables. The same careful matching of resolution, time and measurement meaning applies to other remote-sensing and multi-source analytical problems.
limitations: Satellite aerosol optical depth is not a direct measurement of surface PM2.5. The relationships are statistical and depend on the observation context.
Cloud cover, missing station records and unmodeled meteorology limited the analysis.
Detailed three-product regression figures concern El Salvador; they are not regression models for every Central American country.
Full-period regressions, the 47-month matched comparison and regional poster results use different samples. Their R² values must not be merged or attributed solely to one team member.

evidence.title: El Salvador: product comparisons
evidence.body: These are separate analyses from the final report. Both full-period MODIS relationships were reported as statistically significant at p < 0.001. R² describes explained variation within each stated comparison, not a universal accuracy rating.

evidence.title: Regional poster context
evidence.body: The team poster reports the following country-level simple linear-regression summaries. These are separate from the detailed El Salvador product comparisons. The team also noted elevated AOD and PM2.5 around April and May.

evidence.title: CALIOP–Aqua MODIS consistency
evidence.body: The paired time series generally followed similar patterns and diverged on some dates. It compares lidar and passive satellite aerosol retrievals, rather than directly estimating ground-level PM2.5.
